record.paper_title: Optimal scaling of average queue sizes in an input-queued switch: an open problem
record.original_question: For the maximum weight scheduling policy in the same n by n input-queued switch model, where each time slot chooses a feasible matching that maximizes the sum over scheduled queues of the current queue size, does the steady-state expected total queue size satisfy the same β*_0 = 1 scaling as the conjectured optimum, namely essentially order n/(1 − ρ(λ)) up to constants uniformly over all n and all underloaded arrival-rate matrices?

evidence.quote: The question is whether there exist policies that combine the best features of the above two bounds, i.e., with Q = O(n1+ε/(1 − ρ)) for arbitrarily small ε > 0, and whether this is achieved by the MW policy.
We also have the much stronger conjecture that β∗0 is equal to one even if we restrict to the MW policy.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a discrete-time n×n input-queued switch. There are n input ports and n output ports, with a separate queue Q_{ij}(t) at each input-output pair (i,j), for i,j ∈ {1,...,n}. In each time slot t = 0, 1, 2, ...:

1. New packets arrive: for each (i,j), a Bernoulli(λ_{ij}) number of packets joins Q_{ij}, independently across (i,j) and across time, where λ = (λ_{ij}) is a nonnegative arrival-rate matrix.

2. The scheduler chooses a feasible matching, i.e., a permutation matrix S(t) = (S_{ij}(t)) ∈ {0,1}^{n×n} with each row sum and each column sum equal to 1. If S_{ij}(t) = 1 and Q_{ij}(t) > 0, one packet departs from Q_{ij}.

The arrival-rate matrix λ is called admissible (underloaded) if its maximum row sum and maximum column sum, ρ(λ) := max(max_i Σ_j λ_{ij}, max_j Σ_i λ_{ij}), satisfies ρ(λ) < 1.

The Maximum Weight (MW) policy selects, in each slot t, a permutation matrix S(t) maximizing Σ_{i,j} S_{ij} Q_{ij}(t). Under any admissible λ, this Markov chain is positive recurrent; let Q_{ij}(∞) denote its stationary distribution and define the steady-state expected total queue size
   E_{MW}[|Q|] := Σ_{i,j} E[Q_{ij}(∞)].

Question: Does there exist a constant C < ∞, independent of n and of λ, such that for every n ≥ 1 and every admissible arrival-rate matrix λ with ρ(λ) < 1,
   E_{MW}[|Q|] ≤ C · n / (1 − ρ(λ))^{1+o(1)},
i.e., does the MW policy achieve the conjectured optimal scaling of order n/(1 − ρ(λ)), up to subpolynomial factors, uniformly over all n and all underloaded λ?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the MaxWeight policy achieves optimal Θ(n/(1−ρ)) scaling for the steady-state total queue size in n×n input-queued switches remains open in general. Subsequent works have proved optimal scaling for related but different policies (e.g., via graph factorization, batching-based algorithms) and have established optimality of MaxWeight only in restricted regimes (e.g., when 1−ρ approaches 0 sufficiently fast in n, such as 1−ρ = O(1/n²)). Best known general bounds for MaxWeight remain super-linear in n (improving from O(n³) to O(n^{1.5}(1−ρ)^{-1} log) and O(n^{5/4}(1−ρ)^{-1} log) in various regimes), short of the conjectured n/(1−ρ).

status_evidence.title: Improved Queue-Size Scaling for Input-Queued Switches via Graph Factorization
status_evidence.snippet: A new class of policies achieves expected total queue size O(n^{1.5}(1-ρ)^{-1} log(1/(1-ρ))) in the regime 1-ρ = O(1/n), improving prior bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Best known bounds for MW remain above the conjectured n/(1-ρ); only specialized policies achieve improved scaling, and only in restricted regimes.

status_evidence.title: On Queue-Size Scaling for Input-Queued Switches (arXiv:1405.4764)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the validity of the conjecture for the regime where 1-ρ = O(1/n^2), but the general conjecture for MW remains unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Optimality of MW scaling is established only in restricted heavy-traffic regimes.

status_evidence.title: An algorithm for improved delay-scaling in input-queued switches
status_evidence.snippet: New algorithm with expected total queue length O(n(1-ρ)^{-4/3} log) for uniform arrivals; conjectured optimal n/(1-ρ) MW scaling not proved in general.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent algorithmic work approaches but does not match the conjectured optimal MW scaling.
